prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: The study used data from a population-based cohort survey conducted in Norway between 2017 and 2019.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Out of 5752 randomly selected adults aged 20 or older, 2039 people with complete data were included in the analysis.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: People who had previously suffered a stroke, heart attack, or heart failure were left out of the study.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants' headache types were determined using established questionnaires.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In the initial comparison, people with migraine and tension-type headache had cardiac volumes that were 4% to 15% and 4% to 8% smaller, respectively, than those without headache.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: After accounting for other factors, only tension-type headache was linked to a significantly lower volume in the left ventricle of the heart.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The speed of blood flow into the heart during relaxation was significantly lower in people with migraine with aura.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The results suggest a possible link between tension-type headache and subtle changes in the size of the heart's left chamber.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Migraine with aura was associated with small decreases in blood flow speed, but there was no sign of heart failure.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors state that more research is required to verify these findings and understand their medical importance.
facts.subject: humans
